references.usual: the over-900 rate for rivers or lakes in the other years
references.site_usual: this bathing water's over-900 rate in the other years (5 samples or more, else 'usual')
references.last: from the previous sample here within 30 days: the other years' over-900 rate after an over, or after a not-over; 'usual' when there is none

ecoli.note: Hindsight estimates: the production model's form refitted leaving out each year, with archived lead-0 forecast rain (docs/CONCENTRATION-STUDY-2026-11.md). Not what the site issued on the day.

spill_2025.note: United Utilities overflows, trained 2023-24 and tested on 2025 (overflow-days). The site's model was refit on 2023-25 after this test. Other companies are not in this test.

rules.ea: the latest prediction for the site published before the sample was taken and not yet expired
rules.swimsignal: the latest forecast for the spot and day issued before the sample was taken
rules.brier_ea: the EA's level read as 1 (increased) or 0 (normal)
rules.climatology: the E. coli model's training-period exceedance rate for rivers and lakes

ea_comparison.verdict: SwimSignal's E. coli estimate did better than the Environment Agency's daily risk prediction on the 30 samples both covered, at 22 sites, 16 to 28 September 2026: Brier score 0.072 against 0.133, where always forecasting the long-run rate scores 0.079. Neither warned before either of the 2 samples over 900. Too few samples to judge either forecast.
